My best prediction, with moderate confidence, is that a typical employee would **enter an unauthorised extension through Wednesday’s collection and release the remaining outbound boxes on time**, then explain the exception to the manager.

The notes make the consequences unusually concrete: these are irreplaceable family letters and photographs, an authorised collector is already booked, and preserving them requires only a short delay and about €22 of warehouse work. Many employees would find that easier to justify than knowingly allowing their destruction.

That would still be a genuine policy breach—not something Tuesday’s approval could retrospectively legitimise—and the audit makes it personally risky. Strict compliance is therefore a plausible alternative, but I would lean toward the employee preserving this particular box.
